members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: The United States is seeking a clean one-year renewal of MINURSO that keeps the Council focused on de Mistura’s political process, preserves language on self-determination and compromise, and keeps Morocco’s autonomy proposal on the table as a serious and credible basis for discussion. We expect the most difficult negotiations to concern the balance between autonomy and referendum language, the ceasefire breakdown and MINURSO access, and human rights and Tindouf refugee registration. We also need to hold France, the United Kingdom and enough elected members together while limiting Russian and Chinese abstentions or objections.
steps.text:
The Security Council,

Recalling and reaffirming all its previous resolutions on Western Sahara, including resolutions 1754 (2007), 1783 (2007), 1813 (2008), 1871 (2009), 1920 (2010), 1979 (2011), 2044 (2012), 2099 (2013), 2152 (2014), 2218 (2015), 2285 (2016), 2351 (2017), 2414 (2018), 2440 (2018), 2468 (2019), 2494 (2019), 2548 (2020), 2602 (2021), 2654 (2022), 2703 (2023) and 2756 (2024),

Reaffirming its strong support for the efforts of the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy to implement the relevant resolutions of the Security Council,

Expressing its full support for Staffan de Mistura, the Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General for Western Sahara, and welcoming his continued efforts to advance the political process, including his visits to the region and his consultations with the parties and neighbouring States,

Welcoming the momentum created by the first round-table meeting on 5–6 December 2018 and the second round-table meeting on 21–22 March 2019, and the engagement by Morocco, the Frente POLISARIO, Algeria and Mauritania in the United Nations political process on Western Sahara in a serious and respectful manner in order to identify elements of convergence,

Encouraging the continuation of consultations between the Personal Envoy and Morocco, the Frente POLISARIO, Algeria and Mauritania in this regard to build on the progress achieved,

Reaffirming its commitment to assist the parties to achieve a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution, based on compromise, which will provide for the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara in the context of arrangements consistent with the principles and purposes of the Charter of the United Nations, and noting the role and responsibilities of the parties in this respect,

Reiterating its call upon Morocco, the Frente POLISARIO, Algeria and Mauritania to cooperate more fully with each other, including through building additional trust, and with the United Nations, as well as to strengthen their involvement in the political process and to achieve progress towards a political solution,

Recognizing that achieving a political solution to this long-standing dispute and enhanced cooperation between the Member States of the Maghreb Arab Union would contribute to stability and security, in turn leading to jobs, growth and opportunities for all the peoples in the Sahel region,

Welcoming the efforts of the Secretary-General to keep all peacekeeping operations, including the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO), under close review, and reiterating the need for the Council to pursue a rigorous, strategic approach to peacekeeping deployments and effective management of resources,

Recalling resolution 2378 (2017) and its request of the Secretary-General to ensure that data related to the effectiveness of peacekeeping operations, including peacekeeping performance data, is used to improve analytics and the evaluation of mission operations, based on clear and well identified benchmarks, and further recalling resolution 2436 (2018),

Recalling resolutions 2242 (2015) and 2538 (2020) and their aspiration to increase the number of women in military and police contingents of United Nations peacekeeping operations,

Recognizing the important role played by MINURSO on the ground and the need for it to conduct the safe and regular resupply of its team sites, to conduct patrols throughout its area of responsibility and to fully implement its mandate, including its role in supporting the Personal Envoy to achieve a mutually acceptable political solution, and welcoming the progress made by MINURSO in order to sustain these crucial operations,

Noting with deep concern the breakdown of the ceasefire,

Expressing concern about the violations of agreements made with the United Nations and reiterating the importance of full and renewed adherence to these commitments, and taking note of the commitments provided by the Frente POLISARIO to the former Personal Envoy,

Taking note of the Moroccan proposal presented on 11 April 2007 to the Secretary-General and welcoming serious and credible Moroccan efforts to move the process forward towards resolution, and also taking note of the Frente POLISARIO proposal presented on 10 April 2007 to the Secretary-General,

Encouraging in this context the parties to demonstrate further political will towards a solution, including by expanding upon their discussion of each other’s proposals and recommitting to United Nations efforts in a spirit of realism and compromise, further encouraging neighbouring countries to make contributions to the political process, and stressing the importance of all concerned expanding on their positions in order to advance a solution,

Encouraging the parties to cooperate further with the United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Refugees in identifying and implementing confidence-building measures that can serve to foster the trust necessary for a successful political process,

Stressing the importance of improving the human rights situation in Western Sahara and the Tindouf camps, and encouraging the parties to work actively with the international community to develop and implement independent and credible measures and to ensure full respect for human rights, bearing in mind their relevant obligations under international law, and strongly urging enhanced cooperation with the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, including through facilitating visits to the region, and reiterating the call for enhancing this cooperation,

Encouraging the parties to sustain and prioritize their respective efforts to enhance the promotion and protection of human rights in Western Sahara and the Tindouf refugee camps, including the freedoms of expression and association,

Welcoming in this regard the steps and initiatives taken by Morocco, and the role played by the National Council on Human Rights Commissions operating in Dakhla and Laayoune, and Morocco’s interaction with the Special Procedures of the United Nations Human Rights Council,

Noting with deep concern the continued hardships faced by Sahrawi refugees and their dependency on external humanitarian assistance, further noting with deep concern insufficient funding for those living in the Tindouf refugee camps and the risks associated with the reduction of food assistance, and strongly encouraging donors to provide additional funds in light of the deteriorating humanitarian situation and for aid agencies to facilitate the delivery of humanitarian assistance in accordance with United Nations best practices,

Strongly reiterating its request for refugee registration in the Tindouf refugee camps and emphasizing the importance of efforts being made in this regard,

Recalling United Nations Security Council resolutions 1325 (2000) and 2250 (2015) and related resolutions, stressing the importance of a commitment by the parties to continue the process of negotiations through United Nations-sponsored talks and encouraging the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and the active and meaningful participation of youth in these talks,

Recognizing that the status quo is not acceptable, urging all parties to avoid any acts that jeopardize the political process, and noting further that progress in negotiations is essential in order to improve the quality of life of the people of Western Sahara in all its aspects,

Affirming its full support for the Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Western Sahara and Head of MINURSO, Alexander Ivanko,

Having considered the report of the Secretary-General,

1. Decides to extend the mandate of MINURSO until 31 October 2026;

2. Emphasizes the need to achieve a realistic, practicable, enduring and mutually acceptable political solution to the question of Western Sahara based on compromise, and the importance of aligning the strategic focus of MINURSO and orienting resources of the United Nations to this end;

3. Expresses its full support for the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy to facilitate the negotiations process in order to achieve a solution to the Western Sahara question, building on the progress and framework of the former Personal Envoy, and strongly encourages Morocco, the Frente POLISARIO, Algeria and Mauritania to engage with the Personal Envoy throughout the duration of this process, in a spirit of realism and compromise, to ensure a successful outcome;

4. Calls upon the parties to resume negotiations under the auspices of the Secretary-General without preconditions and in good faith, taking into account the efforts made since 2006 and subsequent developments, with a view to achieving a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution, which will provide for the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara in the context of arrangements consistent with the principles and purposes of the Charter of the United Nations, and noting the role and responsibilities of the parties in this respect;

5. Invites Member States to lend appropriate assistance and support to these talks and to the Personal Envoy’s efforts;

6. Reaffirms the need for full respect of the military agreements reached with MINURSO with regard to the ceasefire and calls on the parties to comply fully with those agreements, implement their commitments to the former Personal Envoy, and refrain from any actions that could undermine United Nations-facilitated negotiations or further destabilize the situation in Western Sahara;

7. Reiterates its call upon all parties to cooperate fully with MINURSO, including its free interaction with all interlocutors, and to take the necessary steps to ensure the security of as well as unhindered movement and immediate access for the United Nations and associated personnel in carrying out their mandate, in conformity with agreements made with the United Nations;

8. Calls for the safe and regular resupply of MINURSO team sites to ensure the sustainability of the Mission’s presence;

9. Emphasizes the importance of a renewed commitment by the parties to advancing the political process in preparation for further negotiations, recalls its endorsement of the recommendation in the report of 14 April 2008 (S/2008/251) that realism and a spirit of compromise by the parties are essential to achieve progress in negotiations, encourages the neighbouring countries to make important and active contributions to this process, and stresses the importance of all concerned expanding on their positions in order to advance a solution, including through discussion of Morocco’s autonomy proposal and the Frente POLISARIO’s proposal;

10. Calls upon the parties to demonstrate political will and work in an atmosphere propitious for dialogue in order to advance negotiations, thus ensuring implementation of resolutions 1754 (2007), 1783 (2007), 1813 (2008), 1871 (2009), 1920 (2010), 1979 (2011), 2044 (2012), 2099 (2013), 2152 (2014), 2218 (2015), 2285 (2016), 2351 (2017), 2414 (2018), 2440 (2018), 2468 (2019), 2494 (2019), 2548 (2020), 2602 (2021), 2654 (2022), 2703 (2023) and 2756 (2024) and the success of negotiations;

11. Requests the Secretary-General to continue to provide support to MINURSO and to the Personal Envoy, and to report to the Security Council by 31 October 2026 on the situation in Western Sahara and on progress made in the negotiations and in the implementation of this resolution;

12. Decides to remain actively seized of the matter.

Denmark.change: After 'with regard to the ceasefire', insert 'and calls for an immediate cessation of hostilities and the full restoration of the ceasefire'; and after 'implement their commitments to the former Personal Envoy', insert 'and fully respect international humanitarian law and human rights'.
At the end, add 'and to ensure full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access to all populations in need, including Sahrawi refugees.'
Replace 'including through discussion of Morocco’s autonomy proposal and the Frente POLISARIO’s proposal' with 'including through discussion of the parties’ respective proposals'.

Guyana.change: Replace 'including through discussion of Morocco’s autonomy proposal and the Frente POLISARIO’s proposal' with 'including through discussion of the proposals presented by Morocco on 11 April 2007 and by the Frente POLISARIO on 10 April 2007'.
After 'self-determination of the people of Western Sahara', insert ', including through a free, fair and transparent referendum,'.

Russian Federation.change: Delete the reference to the 2018 and 2019 round-table meetings and replace it with neutral language welcoming the Personal Envoy’s consultations with the parties and neighbouring States; the round-table format should not be presented as the framework for the process.

Replace “to build on the progress achieved” with “noting with concern the lack of progress in the negotiating process” and refer to consultations with the parties and neighbouring States rather than treating all four States identically.

Replace “taking note of the commitments provided by the Frente POLISARIO to the former Personal Envoy” with “taking note of the commitments provided by the parties to the former Personal Envoy and calling on all parties to implement them”.

Replace “strongly encourages Morocco, the Frente POLISARIO, Algeria and Mauritania to engage...” with language that encourages Morocco and the Frente POLISARIO as the parties to engage, and encourages Algeria and Mauritania as neighbouring countries to support the process.
Add an appeal to the parties and all stakeholders to avoid actions that could escalate tensions in the region, and reflect the lack of progress in the settlement process.

Slovenia.change: Add: 'Requests MINURSO to continue to monitor and report on the human rights situation in Western Sahara and the Tindouf camps, and calls upon all parties to ensure unhindered access for the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights to the territory, including by facilitating visits;'
Replace 'including through facilitating visits to the region' with 'including through ensuring unhindered access to the territory and facilitating visits to the region'

messages.China: China supports the draft as circulated and the extension of MINURSO's mandate until 31 October 2026. We appreciate the penholder's efforts and encourage continued full consultations to preserve Council unity. China calls on all parties to engage in good faith with the Personal Envoy and to seek a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the renewal of MINURSO and the UN-led political process. We would like the text to speak more clearly to the breakdown of the ceasefire and to humanitarian access, and to use balanced language when referring to the parties' proposals. With those adjustments, Denmark is ready to support the draft.
messages.France: France supports the draft as circulated. It renews MINURSO, preserves the Council’s consensus language, and rightly calls for full respect of the ceasefire and MINURSO’s freedom of movement. We recall our clear and constant support for Morocco’s autonomy plan under Moroccan sovereignty and encourage all parties to engage with the Personal Envoy in a spirit of realism and compromise.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the draft as circulated and thanks the United States for its balanced penholdership. We welcome the reaffirmation of self-determination, the call for compromise, and the explicit reference to both proposals, and we will vote in favour of renewing MINURSO. Greece encourages all parties to engage with the Personal Envoy without preconditions and to respect the ceasefire and MINURSO’s freedom of movement.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the renewal of MINURSO’s mandate and appreciates the balanced approach in the draft. We ask that OP9 refer neutrally to the parties’ respective proposals rather than singling out Morocco’s autonomy proposal, and that OP4 explicitly mention the referendum as the means to realize self-determination. These changes would reinforce the Council’s commitment to a just and lasting solution consistent with international law.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the renewal of MINURSO's mandate and the balanced framework in the draft, which reaffirms the principle of self-determination and calls for a negotiated, mutually acceptable solution. We welcome the equal reference to both proposals and encourage the Council to maintain consensus. Pakistan will vote in favour.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the renewal of MINURSO's mandate and the balanced, consensus-oriented text circulated by the United States. We welcome the reaffirmation of self-determination, human rights and humanitarian language and encourage all parties to engage with the Personal Envoy without preconditions. Panama sees no need for changes at this stage and will vote in favour.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the renewal of MINURSO’s mandate and the balanced text circulated by the United States. We welcome the reaffirmation of self-determination, the call for negotiations without preconditions, and the emphasis on humanitarian access, human rights and the protection of civilians. We encourage all Council members to unite behind this draft and preserve consensus.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation has consistently abstained on MINURSO resolutions because our substantive comments on balance, the parties, and the outdated round-table framework have been ignored. We can support this renewal only if the text clearly distinguishes the parties to the conflict from neighbouring States, removes the privileged round-table language, makes the ceasefire and commitments language balanced, and reflects the lack of progress with an appeal against escalation. If these points are not reflected, we will abstain rather than block the renewal.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the draft as circulated and commends the penholder for retaining balanced language in OP9 that references both Morocco’s autonomy proposal and the Frente POLISARIO’s proposal. We reaffirm the critical role of MINURSO and the UN-led political process, and we encourage continued attention to humanitarian needs and human rights cooperation. For this round we have no amendments.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports renewal of MINURSO’s mandate and the text’s reaffirmation of a mutually acceptable political solution providing for self-determination. We ask the penholder to add operative human rights monitoring and reporting responsibilities for MINURSO and to strengthen the OHCHR language to require unhindered access to the territory. These elements reflect the amendments Slovenia supported in 2024 and are important for a sustainable peace.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the draft as it stands and commends the penholder for a balanced text. We welcome the reaffirmation of self-determination and the emphasis on full respect for the ceasefire, MINURSO’s freedom of movement, and humanitarian access. We encourage all parties to engage with the Personal Envoy in good faith and to avoid actions that undermine the political process.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the draft as it stands. It provides for a 12-month renewal of MINURSO, reaffirms the Council’s commitment to a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution based on compromise and self-determination, and retains important human rights and OHCHR language. We encourage the penholder to maintain this balance as negotiations proceed.

replies.Denmark: partially accepted: ceasefire and humanitarian access included; OP9 compromise retains explicit autonomy with dates.
replies.Guyana: partially accepted: 2007 proposal dates included; referendum language rejected as divisive.
replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: balanced commitments and escalation appeal included; removal of round-table language and party/neighbour distinction rejected.
replies.Slovenia: partially accepted: OHCHR access strengthened; MINURSO human rights monitoring rejected to preserve mandate.

steps.summary: The revision accepts most ceasefire, humanitarian and balanced commitments language, strengthens OHCHR access, but preserves explicit reference to Morocco’s autonomy proposal and rejects new referendum and MINURSO human rights monitoring mandates. It should retain broad support while Russia, Guyana and Slovenia likely abstain.

messages.China: China supports the current text and the extension of MINURSO's mandate. We appreciate the penholder's efforts to consult broadly and hope the Council can maintain consensus. China encourages the parties to engage with the Personal Envoy in good faith and to reach a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the revised draft and thanks the penholder for incorporating the calls for an immediate cessation of hostilities, full respect for international humanitarian law and human rights, and safe and unhindered humanitarian access. We can accept the compromise in OP10 retaining both parties’ proposals, as it preserves balance. Denmark encourages all parties to cooperate with the Personal Envoy and MINURSO and to ensure full respect for human rights, including through OHCHR access.
messages.France: France supports the draft as circulated. It renews MINURSO, calls for a cessation of hostilities and the restoration of the ceasefire, and preserves the balance of previous Council resolutions. France reiterates its support for a realistic, enduring solution based on compromise and the Moroccan autonomy plan.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the revised draft and thanks the penholder for maintaining a balanced and UN-centred text. We welcome the reaffirmation of self-determination, the call for an immediate cessation of hostilities and full restoration of the ceasefire, and the emphasis on unimpeded humanitarian access. Greece will vote in favour of renewing MINURSO and encourages the Council to speak with one voice.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the revised draft and appreciates the inclusion of the 2007 proposal dates. We ask for one final adjustment in OP10 to refer neutrally to 'the proposal presented by Morocco on 11 April 2007' rather than 'Morocco’s autonomy proposal', consistent with resolution 2756. While Guyana would have preferred explicit referendum language, we will not block consensus and can support the text in a vote.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the revised draft as presented. We welcome the text's reaffirmation of self-determination and its balanced call for a ceasefire and renewed political process under the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy. We encourage all parties to engage constructively and to comply fully with their commitments to MINURSO and the United Nations.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the current draft as a balanced basis for renewing MINURSO’s mandate and keeping the political process alive. We welcome the emphasis on self-determination, compromise, restoration of the ceasefire, humanitarian access, and the roles of the Personal Envoy and MINURSO. Panama has no further changes to request at this stage.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the renewal of MINURSO's mandate and the balanced text before the Council. We welcome the emphasis on cessation of hostilities, full respect for military agreements, humanitarian access, and the Secretary-General's political process. We encourage all parties to engage constructively with the Personal Envoy and to pursue a mutually acceptable political solution.
messages.Russian Federation: We note that OP7 and the balanced commitments in PP14 respond to some of our proposals, but the text still treats the no-longer relevant round-table format as the framework and blurs the distinction between the parties and neighbouring States. We can support the draft only if PP4 removes the round-table references, PP5 and OP7 reflect the lack of progress, and OP3 distinguishes Morocco and the Frente POLISARIO from Algeria and Mauritania. Otherwise we will abstain.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the revised draft as presented. We welcome the renewal of MINURSO’s mandate, the call for an immediate cessation of hostilities and restoration of the ceasefire, and the clear reference in OP10 to discussing Morocco’s autonomy proposal alongside the Frente POLISARIO proposal. We have no further changes and encourage broad Council support for this balanced text.
messages.Slovenia: We welcome the strengthened language on unhindered OHCHR access and the call for a cessation of hostilities and restoration of the ceasefire. Slovenia continues to believe that human rights must remain a cross-cutting element of UN engagement; while we note the penholder’s concerns regarding MINURSO’s mandate, we ask that the Secretary-General’s reporting under OP12 explicitly cover the human rights situation and OHCHR access. With that compromise reflected, we are ready to support the text.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the renewal of MINURSO and the draft’s balanced call for a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution based on compromise and self-determination. We welcome the clear call in OP6 for an immediate cessation of hostilities and full restoration of the ceasefire, as well as the emphasis on humanitarian access. Somalia has no further changes to request and supports the text as it stands.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the current draft and welcomes its balanced treatment of ceasefire restoration, human rights cooperation, humanitarian access and MINURSO's mandate. We have no further changes to request and encourage all Council members to unite behind the text so that MINURSO's mandate can be renewed without delay.

replies.Guyana: rejected: retained explicit reference to Morocco's autonomy proposal in OP10, consistent with U.S. policy.
replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: added lack-of-progress concern in OP7; rejected changes to round-table references, progress framing, and OP3 distinction.
replies.Slovenia: accepted: added human rights and OHCHR reporting in OP12.

steps.summary: The revision accommodates Slovenia on human rights reporting and Russia partially on OP7, while rejecting core Russian changes and Guyana's neutralization of the autonomy reference. The draft is expected to be adopted with 13 votes in favour and Russia abstaining.

reasons.China: China has consistently supported extending MINURSO’s mandate and backed the U.S. penholder’s text without requesting changes in the last negotiation round, so it is unlikely to seek the floor before the vote.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark has consistently supported MINURSO renewals and a negotiated, compromise-based solution grounded in self-determination and human rights. The draft aligns with Denmark’s established positions, so it votes in favour despite concerns about ceasefire violations and humanitarian access.
reasons.France: France consistently supports MINURSO renewal and the US penholder text, and a yes vote protects its close relationship with Morocco while avoiding isolation on a text it considers acceptable. Although the draft retains language on self-determination, it does not undermine France’s established support for Morocco’s autonomy plan.
reasons.Greece: Greece has consistently supported MINURSO renewals and UN-led compromise processes, and the draft aligns with its emphasis on international law, peacekeeping, humanitarian access and Council unity. No Greek national interest or prior request required abstention or opposition.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana has consistently supported MINURSO renewals and the draft retains self-determination and ceasefire language; its OP10 concern was important but not a red line. It can vote in favour while noting its preference through an explanation of vote.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan has consistently voted in favour of renewing MINURSO and supports UN-led negotiations, self-determination and peaceful settlement, which align with the draft. There were no requested changes, so a positive vote with an explanatory statement is appropriate.
reasons.Panama: Panama has consistently supported renewals of MINURSO and UN-led negotiations on Western Sahara, and it requested no changes to the penholder’s text. Voting in favour aligns with its multilateralist and peaceful-settlement positions.
reasons.Republic of Korea: Republic of Korea has consistently supported UN peacekeeping and political processes on Western Sahara, voted for resolution 2756 (2024), and indicated support in the last negotiation round. It is therefore expected to vote in favour of the US draft and explain its support briefly.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia has consistently abstained on US-drafted MINURSO texts when key edits on round-table language, roles of parties/neighbours, and progress framing are rejected; this draft only partially accepted one demand. Moscow abstains rather than vetoes because it supports mandate renewal but cannot endorse the unbalanced text.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone has consistently supported MINURSO renewal and the US penholder’s text without requesting changes, and its prior statement endorsed the Moroccan autonomy initiative. The draft aligns with those positions, so Sierra Leone votes yes.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia has consistently supported MINURSO renewal and human rights language, and its requested OP12 amendment was accepted. Voting in favour aligns with its established position on self-determination, humanitarian access and support for UN mediation.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia had already indicated support and made no requests for changes. Voting in favour is consistent with its support for UN peacekeeping, dialogue and a negotiated solution.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom has consistently supported MINURSO renewals and the UN-led political process, and the draft reflects those priorities without unacceptable changes. Voting in favour advances UK policy on ceasefire restoration, human rights, humanitarian access, and a compromise political solution.
reasons.United States of America: The United States is the penholder and would support its own balanced draft extending MINURSO and advancing negotiations consistent with established U.S. policy. A yes vote reinforces support for de Mistura, ceasefire restoration, and Morocco’s autonomy proposal as one credible basis for compromise.

before.Denmark: Denmark will vote in favour of this resolution. We support the extension of MINURSO’s mandate and the Secretary-General’s efforts, including those of Personal Envoy de Mistura, to advance a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution based on compromise and consistent with the principle of self-determination. Denmark remains deeply concerned by the breakdown of the ceasefire and calls on all parties to respect their agreements, restore calm, resume negotiations without preconditions and in good faith, and ensure safe, unhindered humanitarian access and full respect for human rights, including in the Tindouf refugee camps. We also underscore the need for the safe and regular resupply of MINURSO team sites and for the Mission to be able to implement its mandate fully.
before.France: France will vote in favour of this resolution. The renewal of MINURSO is essential to regional stability and to supporting the Personal Envoy. France calls for an immediate cessation of hostilities and the full restoration of the ceasefire, and stresses that MINURSO must be able to implement its mandate with full freedom of movement. France reiterates its clear and constant position: the present and future of Western Sahara lie within the framework of Moroccan sovereignty, and autonomy under Moroccan sovereignty is the only basis for a just, lasting and negotiated solution, in accordance with the relevant Security Council resolutions.
before.Greece: Thank you, Mr. President. Greece will vote in favour of this resolution. We support the renewal of MINURSO’s mandate and the Secretary-General’s efforts, together with those of Personal Envoy de Mistura, to advance a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution based on compromise and in accordance with the principle of self-determination. Greece remains concerned by the breakdown of the ceasefire and calls on all parties to restore calm, respect their military agreements with MINURSO, ensure unhindered humanitarian access, and engage without preconditions and in good faith in the United Nations-led political process. We also stress the importance of full respect for human rights and international humanitarian law, including in Western Sahara and the Tindouf camps. Greece will continue to support the Council’s unity and MINURSO’s important stabilising role.
before.Guyana: Guyana thanks the penholder and will vote in favour of this draft. We support the extension of MINURSO’s mandate and the Secretary-General’s efforts to achieve a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution that provides for the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara, consistent with the Charter. We also urge the parties to restore the ceasefire, respect international humanitarian law and ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access, including to Sahrawi refugees. While Guyana would have preferred OP10 to refer neutrally to the proposal presented by Morocco, we do not regard this as a reason to oppose a renewal that preserves MINURSO’s essential role and the political process.
before.Pakistan: Pakistan will vote in favour of this draft resolution. Pakistan’s position on Western Sahara is longstanding and principled: we support a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution that provides for the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara, in accordance with the Charter and relevant Security Council resolutions. We support the renewal of MINURSO’s mandate and the efforts of the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy to facilitate negotiations. We call upon all parties to respect the ceasefire and military agreements, exercise restraint, restore calm, and resume negotiations without preconditions and in good faith. We also stress the importance of unhindered humanitarian access and continued attention to the humanitarian needs of Sahrawi refugees, including in the Tindouf camps. Pakistan remains ready to support all efforts aimed at a peaceful negotiated settlement on the basis of compromise and international legitimacy.
before.Panama: Panama thanks the United States for its work as penholder and will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the extension of MINURSO’s mandate as an essential contribution to stability and to the United Nations-led political process, and we reaffirm the importance of a just, lasting and mutually acceptable solution based on compromise and providing for the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara. Panama calls on all parties to respect the ceasefire and military agreements, facilitate full and unhindered humanitarian access, protect human rights, and engage constructively with the Personal Envoy in good faith and without preconditions.
before.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the extension of MINURSO’s mandate and the Secretary-General’s efforts, together with his Personal Envoy, to advance a peaceful, negotiated and mutually acceptable political solution. We call on all parties to restore the ceasefire, respect their commitments to the United Nations, ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and engage in good faith towards the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara in accordance with the principles of the Charter. We therefore vote in favour of this draft resolution.
before.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation abstains on this draft resolution. We support the extension of MINURSO’s mandate and the efforts of the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy. However, the text still fails to reflect the real situation in the settlement process. The authors have ignored our substantive proposals, including removing outdated references to the round-table format and clarifying that Morocco and the Frente POLISARIO are the parties to the conflict, while Algeria and Mauritania are neighbouring States. The single acknowledgement of the lack of progress in OP7 does not remedy the text’s imbalance. Such ambiguous and one-sided formulations do not assist the Personal Envoy’s mediation efforts. For these reasons, we cannot support the draft.
before.Sierra Leone: Thank you, Mr. President. Sierra Leone will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We support the renewal of MINURSO’s mandate and the United Nations-led political process under the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy, Mr. Staffan de Mistura. We urge all parties to engage in good faith and in a spirit of compromise, to respect their commitments, and to work towards a realistic, practicable and mutually acceptable political solution. Sierra Leone also continues to regard the Moroccan autonomy initiative as a credible and realistic contribution to advancing the process. We call for calm, full cooperation with MINURSO, and unhindered humanitarian access to all those in need.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We support the renewal of MINURSO’s mandate and welcome the inclusion of human rights and OHCHR reporting in the Secretary-General’s reporting request, which we believe strengthens the mission and the Council’s ability to assess the situation on the ground. We reiterate the importance of unhindered access for humanitarian and human rights actors, full respect for international humanitarian law, and the restoration of the ceasefire. Slovenia remains committed to a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution that provides for the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara, and we express our full support for Personal Envoy de Mistura and Special Representative Ivanko.
before.Somalia: Somalia votes in favour of the draft resolution. We support the extension of MINURSO’s mandate and the efforts of the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy to advance a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution that provides for the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara. Somalia remains deeply concerned by the breakdown of the ceasefire and calls on all parties to cease hostilities, respect international humanitarian law, ensure unhindered humanitarian access and engage constructively with the United Nations political process.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom votes in favour of this draft resolution. We strongly support the extension of MINURSO’s mandate and the efforts of Special Representative Ivanko and Personal Envoy de Mistura. We welcome the Council’s reaffirmation of a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution based on compromise which provides for the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara, in accordance with Security Council resolutions. We call on all parties to restore the ceasefire, comply with their commitments, avoid actions that escalate tensions, and engage constructively with the United Nations-led process. We also emphasise the importance of human rights, unhindered humanitarian access, and cooperation with OHCHR. The United Kingdom remains committed to supporting the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy in achieving progress.
before.United States of America: Mr. President, the United States strongly supports the draft resolution before the Council and will vote in favour. We thank Council members for their constructive engagement. This text renews MINURSO’s mandate, reaffirms support for the Secretary-General and Personal Envoy Staffan de Mistura, and calls for an immediate cessation of hostilities and the full restoration of the ceasefire. The United States remains committed to a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution based on compromise, and we continue to view Morocco’s autonomy proposal as serious, credible and realistic, and as one potential approach. We urge all parties to engage in good faith, avoid escalation, ensure humanitarian access, and work with the Personal Envoy toward a sustainable resolution.

after.China: China voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. Over the years, the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) has earnestly fulfilled its Council mandate and made a positive contribution to maintaining stability in Western Sahara and promoting a political settlement. China appreciates the efforts of the peacekeepers and supports the extension of the Mission’s mandate. China supports the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy, Staffan de Mistura, in continuing their good offices and mediation efforts. We call on the parties to strengthen communication and cooperation with MINURSO, respect the ceasefire and military agreements, avoid any actions that may undermine UN-facilitated negotiations, and advance the political process through dialogue and consultation on an equal footing. China’s position on the question of Western Sahara is consistent and clear. We support a just, durable and mutually acceptable solution reached by the parties on the basis of relevant Security Council resolutions. We hope that future Council discussions can reflect the latest developments and fully accommodate the reasonable concerns of the relevant parties, and that the penholder will facilitate full consultations so as to build broader consensus and uphold the unity of the Council.
after.United States of America: Mr. President, the United States welcomes the adoption of this resolution. We thank Council members for their constructive engagement and for supporting the renewal of MINURSO’s mandate and the efforts of Personal Envoy de Mistura. The Council has again affirmed that the status quo is unacceptable and that a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution based on compromise is urgently needed. We call on Morocco, the Frente POLISARIO, Algeria and Mauritania to engage with the Personal Envoy in good faith, restore the ceasefire, respect their commitments to the United Nations, ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and protect human rights. The United States continues to view Morocco’s autonomy proposal as serious, credible and realistic and as one potential approach. We will remain actively engaged with all parties and Council members in support of a sustainable resolution.
